name: Streamlined Onboard & Launch
description: Get a company live fast without letting page-created preview products escape into production. Source discovery finalizes and canonically imports the product catalog before any page work starts. A post-import destination baseline then detects every product created by page steps; any new product blocks theme publication and emits a remediation plan because the current importer cannot prove full equivalence when adopting an existing preview. Page-review findings still flow to the handoff. Themes are built by Fable 5. For the trimmed single-model version, use Speed Import.

steps.name: Business details, markets, and reputation
steps.prompt:
Fill in what Fluid needs to know about this company. Call run_skill("onboarding/onboarding-prefill") and follow it.

Cover the onboarding form in ONE pass over onboarding_info: legal and trading name, support contact, business hours, address, the selling countries and currencies the source actually serves, and public reputation (Trustpilot / BBB) when a profile is genuinely the same company — same registrable domain, or exact legal name plus address. A namesake is not a match; record it as not found.

GET onboarding_info before you PUT and deep-merge, because PUT replaces the whole blob. Do not echo back an empty optional nested object. This is the only step in the run that writes onboarding_info, so nothing else can clobber you — but that also means anything you skip stays empty.

Best effort throughout. A field the public site does not state is an entry in unresolved, not a guess and not a reason to stop. Never pause to ask the operator a question.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { fields_written: [...], countries: [...], reputation: {...}, unresolved: [...] }.
acceptance: onboarding_info was read before it was written and the write merged rather than replaced existing human-entered values.
Every persisted business fact traces to the source site or an identity-matched public record; unverifiable fields are listed in unresolved rather than filled with placeholders.

steps.name: Capture the source site
steps.prompt:
Capture the source site once, well, so every later page step builds from evidence instead of re-crawling. Call run_skill("themes/theme-source-inventory") and follow it.

Scope: the home page in full, plus a route inventory — which pages exist, what each one is, and the canonical URL for shop, one product, one collection or category, and the main content pages. Do NOT deep-capture every route here; the page steps capture their own.

Capture home with formats ["html", "rawHtml", "screenshot"] and capturePageEvidence: true at desktop AND at 390 wide. That retains three things the page steps depend on: the site's own CSS labelled by origin, resolved computed styles for every text landmark, and signed screenshots. Confirm in your output that the stylesheet document and the landmark style table are actually on disk — a note that says CSS was retained is not the same as a file.

Write clone-manifest.json with the route map and the evidence paths.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { routes: {...}, evidence: { stylesheet_path, sidecar_path, landmark_styles: <count>, screenshots: [...] }, unresolved: [...] }.

steps.name: Baseline products after canonical import
steps.prompt:
Create the read-only, run-scoped product baseline after canonical import succeeds and before any page step can run. This ordering is the safety boundary: a later gate treats every product absent from this baseline as page-created and blocks publication. Do not create, update, or delete a Fluid product.

Read import-products STEP_OUTPUT and require status: complete, coverage_percent: 100, and zero failures. This is only identity-level completion; do not claim that the importer verified full title, description, price, option, variant-topology, or product-image equivalence.

Generate a fresh UUID as run_id and create `.mist-desktop/streamlined-preview-products/<run_id>/`. Set baseline_catalog_index_path to `<that-directory>/baseline-catalog-index.json`, then call `fluid_catalog_index({ output_path: <exact baseline_catalog_index_path>, verify_only: false })` exactly once. This built-in capability cursor-paginates GET /api/v202604/company/products?page[limit]=100 through every exact meta.pagination.next_cursor until null, rejects duplicate ids and repeated cursors, writes a complete index atomically, and spot-checks product details without loading every page into model context. Do not replace it with manual page calls.

Read its compact receipt and require status: written_and_verified, complete: true, next_cursor: null, duplicate_count: 0, and matching page/product counts. Re-read the index, preserve each API-returned product id exactly as baseline_product_ids, and require product_count to equal the number of unique ids.

Write `baseline.json` in that directory with version, run_id, captured_at, import_manifest_sha256, baseline_catalog_index_path, baseline_catalog_index_sha256, destination_pages, baseline_product_ids, product_count, and final_cursor:null. Re-read both files and use one `file_sha256` call to compute their raw SHA-256 digests.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { run_id, preview_product_ledger_dir, baseline_path, baseline_sha256, baseline_catalog_index_path, baseline_catalog_index_sha256, import_manifest_sha256, destination_pages, baseline_products, final_cursor: null }.
acceptance: Canonical import completed before the baseline, and no product-capable page step can start until this baseline succeeds.

The worker used one fluid_catalog_index write call for the run-scoped baseline; its receipt proves every v202604 cursor was followed to null, counts balance, no duplicate id or repeated cursor was accepted, and every exact product id is recorded.

The reviewer independently re-read baseline.json and baseline-catalog-index.json, hashed both with file_sha256, and called fluid_catalog_index with verify_only:true against the exact baseline_catalog_index_path. A missing/drifted file, incomplete cursor walk, identity mismatch, or failed spot-check is QA_VERDICT: FAIL.

steps.name: Build the home page
steps.prompt:
Build the home page from the retained source evidence and the existing theme code. This step implements the page; screenshots are not a correctness gate.

Read clone-manifest.json first, then read the retained source HTML, source CSS, resolved landmark styles, and exact stable copy for Home. Retained source screenshots are optional, non-authoritative design input only. You may open only the retained source screenshot paths from clone-manifest.json with view_project_image as design context. Do not capture new or local screenshots and do not call screenshot_preview or compare_preview_to_source.

Inspect the existing layout, shared header, shared footer, tokens, sections, blocks, components, and assets before editing. Reuse the shared shell and existing canonical components where they fit. Build the source order as multiple named Liquid sections mounted separately in home_page/default/index.liquid; never replace it with one monolithic page-sized section.

Copy every stable source heading, paragraph, label, and CTA exactly. Bind products, collections, prices, images, routes, cart controls, and other resource/dynamic content through Fluid Liquid data and existing Fluid hooks rather than hardcoding the observed example. Keep editor-manageable section schemas and normal responsive document flow.

Deliver the home media in bulk before wiring sections to it. Write the home media inventory into clone-manifest.json under priority_media.items, creating the key if absent; no earlier streamlined step owns it. Record one item per unique required media element: source_url plus route, media_kind, landmark, and viewport_role, with poster and playback attributes for video, and source_url: null plus a concrete source_unavailable_reason when an element's bytes are genuinely not fetchable. theme_media_reconcile always reads a catalog index; when fluid-catalog-index.json does not exist in the project sandbox, write {"products":[],"complete":true,"next_cursor":null,"product_count":0} to .mist-desktop/home-catalog-index.json and pass that stub path. Never write the stub to the default fluid-catalog-index.json path; the stub declares catalog matching out of scope for this step, not that the company has no products.

Then call theme_media_reconcile exactly once with manifest_path: "clone-manifest.json", catalog_index_path set to the real index when it exists and the stub path otherwise, mode: "theme_only", and verify_only: false. It uploads missing assets in batches, HEAD-verifies every delivery URL, and checkpoints the manifest as it goes; if it is interrupted or reports a transient upload failure, call it again with identical input and it resumes from verified receipts without re-uploading completed sources. Reference home media in Liquid through the verified delivery URLs it records in priority_media.delivery_items, keeping image_picker overrides so sections stay editor-manageable. Do not replace the reconcile call with dozens of manual dam_upload calls; reserve dam_upload for a straggler asset discovered after reconciliation.

Reject base-theme scaffold filler, lorem text, placeholder products or images, inline binary media (data: or base64), hardcoded development theme ids, generated company hostnames, localhost ports, query-triggered QA shortcuts, and absolute environment-specific asset URLs. Do not use fixed or absolute whole-section relocation, page-height clamps, overflow clipping, hidden/cropped source content, transparent duplicates, or other layout-hiding hacks to simulate correctness.

Run fluid theme lint --json and fix every error. Use the local preview only for deterministic runtime checks: read the rendered DOM for `/`, browser console, and local server logs. Verify HTTP success, source-ordered sections and stable copy, Fluid-bound dynamic content, shared-shell reuse, and no runtime/resource failures. Do not take or compare local screenshots.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { files_read: [...], files_changed: [...], sections: [...], stable_copy_checked: [...], dynamic_bindings: [...], lint: {...}, dom_checks: [...], console_errors: [...], server_errors: [...], media_delivery: { items: <count>, delivered: <count>, source_inline: <count>, source_unavailable: <count> }, unresolved: [...] }.
acceptance: The independent reviewer read clone-manifest.json plus at least three distinct implementation files, including home_page/default/index.liquid and the separately mounted section or shared-shell files it references.
The independent reviewer ran fluid theme lint --json in read-only mode and it returned zero errors.
Targeted code searches found multiple named section mounts in source order, exact stable source copy, Fluid-backed resource/dynamic bindings, and shared-shell reuse.
Targeted code searches found no base-theme scaffold filler, inline binary media, hardcoded environment identity, monolithic page-sized section, or layout-hiding workaround.
The independent reviewer read the local rendered DOM for / in all mode and confirmed HTTP success, multiple source-ordered sections, stable copy, dynamic bindings, and shared shell output.

The independent reviewer read the priority_media block of clone-manifest.json and confirmed a completed priority_media reconciliation: delivery items carry verified DAM delivery URLs with zero unreconciled entries, and the rendered DOM serves home media from those delivery URLs rather than empty media slots for delivered items.
The independent reviewer read the preview console and local server logs and found no unresolved Liquid, runtime, resource, or browser errors.

steps.name: Publish the theme
steps.prompt:
Publish the built theme so the storefront is live.

1. Re-read the touched templates and confirm no scaffold filler survived — placeholder names, lorem text, and the starter theme's own copy all count.
2. Resolve both theme identities and record them: the development theme the preview has been using, and the release target. They are not the same theme.
3. Push and activate the release target, then GET /api/application_themes/active and confirm the active id is the one you just pushed.
4. Default-template audit (required). From the same GET /api/application_themes/active response, group the theme's templates by themeable_type and require a default:true entry for every type the storefront routes through: layouts, home_page, navbar, footer, product, collection, category, page, post, cart_page, shop_page, locales. A missing default:true template for a routed themeable_type is exactly what makes a live route render as HTTP 204 with an empty body. A theme MAY legitimately lack one of these types only if a working reference theme (one whose live routes render) shows the same gap. If a default is missing, fix it — mark the right template default:true or create it — and re-run this audit until it passes; do not report the gap and move on.
5. Load the live home URL and one product route in the browser and record, for each route, the HTTP status AND the response body byte count. Every checked route must return 200 with a non-empty rendered body and must not redirect to home. A 204, or any empty body, IS a failed publish — the theme is not live no matter what the activation API said. "The storefront QA step will catch it" is not an excuse to pass this step; fix the cause (almost always a missing default template from the audit above) and re-verify until every route returns 200 with a real body.
6. Confirm the header logo and any brand imagery in the templates resolve to Fluid DAM URLs, not the source site's CDN. The theme track builds from the source and does not wait on the brand step, so a source-CDN logo can survive into the templates; those links rot and leak the source domain. Repoint any that slipped through to the DAM URL the brand step persisted.


If a page step earlier in this run finished with findings, publish anyway and carry those findings into your output. Shipping a storefront with a known rough edge beats leaving the company with nothing live.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { development_theme_id, release_theme_id, active_theme_id, live_url, default_template_audit: {types_verified: [...], types_fixed: [...]}, routes_checked: [{route, status, body_bytes}], carried_findings: [...] }.
acceptance: The active application theme id equals the theme this run built and pushed.

The active theme has a default:true template for every routed themeable_type (layouts, home_page, navbar, footer, product, collection, category, page, post, cart_page, shop_page, locales), or a working reference theme demonstrably lacks the same type.

The live home route and at least one product route were checked with recorded HTTP status and body byte count per route, and every checked route returned 200 with a non-empty body — a 204 or empty body fails this step.
No template references the source site's CDN for the logo or brand imagery; those assets resolve to Fluid DAM URLs.

steps.name: Map the source catalog
steps.prompt:
Build and finalize the complete product source manifest before anything writes to Fluid. Call run_skill("fluid-product-admin-import") and follow its catalog completion contract. This step is read-only against Fluid.

Read clone-manifest.json before discovery. Treat every distinct product or shop origin in its route inventory as a catalog root. Discovery across those roots is one union: do not narrow the denominator to the launcher website's host when the source inventory found a separate shop or PDP host.

WRITE AS YOU GO — this step's real constraint is your context window, not the network. Fetching a thousand product pages and holding them in the conversation exceeds the model's prompt limit, and that is a hard turn error. Persist discovery and enrichment as separate state, never as duplicate event rows in one manifest.

Use three distinct artifacts:
1. Discover identities first and write each exactly once to `catalog-identities.jsonl`, holding only source_url, source_id, source_handle, and title. This ordered identity index is the denominator. Never append an enriched product row to catalog-identities.jsonl. Reject duplicate source identities and handles while writing it.
2. Enrich in batches of at most 20. After extracting one complete product, write one importer-complete record per identity atomically to `catalog-records/<sha256(source_id)>.json`; a retry replaces that identity's record atomically instead of appending another event. Include title, description, price, currency, image_urls, option_axes, every variant identity/options/price/SKU, and collection membership. Never keep a fetched page body in context once its fields are extracted.
3. Only after discovery is exhausted, stream the ordered identity index and its records into a new immutable importer-valid JSON object at `catalog-manifest.json`. Each index identity must resolve to exactly one record; missing, extra, identity-only, duplicate-identity, duplicate-handle, malformed, or unresolved records make status: BLOCKED. Include source_market_iso, products, excluded, discovery evidence, and unresolved. Re-read the finalized manifest, validate its counts and uniqueness, then compute manifest_sha256. Never append to the finalized manifest.

Prefer cheap, structured sources over full pages: a products JSON endpoint, JSON-LD, or embedded application state carries the same fields at a fraction of the size. When you must fetch a PDP, request markdown rather than html or rawHtml — you need field values here, not layout. Layout is the theme track's problem and it captures its own evidence.

Discovery is still a union, not a sample: sitemap.xml and every child sitemap; any structured catalog API, exhausted to its own terminator; every collection and category pagination followed to the end; then every unique product enriched. A batch size is transport chunking, never a completion limit. A collection that ended in a network error is not exhausted — retry it, and if it still will not enumerate, record it in unresolved with the exact error.

If context is running out, leave catalog-identities.jsonl and the atomic catalog-records/ checkpoints intact and return status: BLOCKED. Do not fabricate a complete manifest and do not permit import to start.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { status: complete|BLOCKED, identity_index_path, records_dir, manifest_path, manifest_sha256, products: <count>, enriched: <count>, identity_only: <count>, variants: <count>, collections: <count>, completeness_basis: "…", unresolved: [...] }.
acceptance: Catalog discovery ran as a union of sitemap, API, and pagination sources rather than a top-N sample, and the manifest states how completeness was established.

catalog-identities.jsonl contains one identity row per discovered product, catalog-records/ contains one importer-complete atomic record per identity, and catalog-manifest.json contains each identity exactly once with no unresolved or identity-only rows.

steps.name: Block page-created preview products
steps.prompt:
Fail closed before theme publication if any page step created a product after canonical import. This is a read-only Fluid audit plus local evidence write. Do not call fluid_product_import and do not create, update, publish, unpublish, or delete products. The current importer can adopt a slug/SKU match without proving full field, option, variant-topology, or product-image equivalence, so this workflow must never ask it to reconcile a page-created preview.

Read the exact run_id, preview_product_ledger_dir, baseline_path, baseline_sha256, baseline_catalog_index_path, and baseline_catalog_index_sha256 from preview-product-ledger STEP_OUTPUT. Re-read both baseline files, recompute both hashes with file_sha256, and stop on drift. Read the Shop, Product, and Collection STEP_OUTPUT values only as attribution evidence; they cannot authorize adoption or repair.

Set current_catalog_index_path to `<preview_product_ledger_dir>/gate-current-catalog-index.json`, then call `fluid_catalog_index({ output_path: <exact current_catalog_index_path>, verify_only: false })` exactly once. Read its compact receipt and require status: written_and_verified, complete: true, next_cursor: null, duplicate_count: 0, and balanced page/product counts. The capability cursor-paginates GET /api/v202604/company/products?page[limit]=100 through every exact meta.pagination.next_cursor until null and rejects repeated cursors, duplicate ids, a missing terminator, or a truncated page. Do not replace it with manual page calls.

Re-read the current index and compute the exact destination-id difference against baseline_product_ids. Every product id absent from the post-import baseline is a run-created candidate. GET each candidate's detail and write `preview-products.json` in preview_product_ledger_dir with run_id, fluid_product_id, returned slug/canonical route, raw lifecycle/public fields, and page-output attribution evidence when available. Never match by title alone, list position, fuzzy URL, or neighboring product.

The policy is zero tolerance: any run-created product makes status: BLOCKED, regardless of attribution, lifecycle status, apparent completeness, or source match. Do not exclude, adopt, enrich, repair, delete, or pass through a candidate. For a blocked result, write `preview-product-remediation-plan.json` beside the ledger with run_id, baseline/current/new counts, preview_product_ledger_path, exact Fluid ids, observed fields, attribution evidence, and the required human/cross-repository follow-up. Publication may proceed only when run_created_products == 0; a complete result has remediation_plan_path: null.

Write `preview-product-gate-receipt.json` with the baseline and current index paths/hashes, status, counts, and unresolved evidence errors. Re-read the baseline, current index, receipt, and any remediation plan, require the counts to balance, then hash the current index and receipt with file_sha256. Report status: complete only for a cursor-complete destination audit with zero run-created products and zero unresolved evidence errors.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { status: complete|BLOCKED, run_id, preview_product_ledger_path, baseline_sha256, baseline_catalog_index_path, baseline_catalog_index_sha256, current_catalog_index_path, current_catalog_index_sha256, gate_receipt_path, gate_receipt_sha256, run_created_products, remediation_plan_path: null|<path>, baseline_products, current_products, unresolved: [...] }.
acceptance: The reviewer re-read the exact run-scoped baseline, current catalog index, and gate receipt, verified their recorded hashes with file_sha256, and independently called fluid_catalog_index with verify_only:true against the exact current_catalog_index_path; the live v202604 catalog is cursor-complete to null with balanced counts and no duplicate id or repeated cursor.
Every product id absent from the post-import baseline is recorded in the run-scoped preview ledger with its exact Fluid id.
Any page-created candidate blocks publication; attribution, inactive status, or apparent source parity never turns a run-created product into a pass.

PASS BAR: QA_VERDICT: PASS requires STEP_OUTPUT status: complete, zero run-created products (run_created_products == 0), unresolved: [], balanced counts, unchanged baseline hashes, and remediation_plan_path: null. Any status: BLOCKED, nonzero candidate count, unresolved entry, or remediation result containing a product id is QA_VERDICT: FAIL and onFail: stop prevents publication.

A blocked gate writes a remediation plan with exact Fluid ids and evidence but performs no product mutation or importer call; correct remediation evidence does not turn the required QA_VERDICT: FAIL into a pass.

steps.name: Import products
steps.prompt:
Canonically import the finalized source catalog before any product-capable page step runs. Read the exact manifest_path and manifest_sha256 from catalog-manifest STEP_OUTPUT and require its status: complete, identity_only: 0, and zero unresolved; do not substitute an identity index, records directory, different hash, or narrower catalog.

Call `fluid_product_import({ manifest_path: <exact manifest_path>, manifest_sha256: <exact manifest_sha256> })` exactly once in write mode. Do not set `verify_only:true`. The built-in tool owns manifest validation, market resolution, image uploads, product writes, bounded retries, checkpoint/resume, and identity-level live reconciliation. Do not invoke lower-level API or DAM tools and do not build a manual product or image loop.

Read the compact receipt. Require status: complete, coverage_percent: 100, zero failures, and exactly one outcome for every finalized-manifest identity. This receipt proves identity-level completion only: current duplicate adoption and verify-only behavior do not prove full title, description, price, option, variant-topology, or product-image equivalence for a pre-existing match. Return the compact receipt as STEP_OUTPUT without expanding the manifest.
acceptance: Every product in the source manifest resolves to exactly one live Fluid product — no duplicates, no silent drops — and the identity-level verification count is proven by paginating the products API rather than by self-report.
The receipt explicitly states that identity-level verification does not prove full field fidelity for a pre-existing match; strengthening that importer contract is separate cross-repository work.

steps.name: Import pages, posts, and menus
steps.prompt:
Create the non-product storefront resources the source has, so the theme's routes have real data behind them. Call run_skill("fluid-product-admin-import") first and follow its contract for these resource types.

In scope: collections and their membership, categories where the source has a genuine curated taxonomy, content pages, blog posts, and the navigation menus that link them.

A page's body is the point of importing it. Shopify's `body_html` is empty on every section-built or page-builder page — the copy lives in template sections — so `body_html` alone silently imports an empty page and reports it as a success. For each page: if `body_html` is empty, fetch the page's rendered DOM and take the main content region instead. Only when the RENDERED page is also empty is the source page genuinely empty; record those in `empty_at_source` with the URL and what was rendered. Never publish a page whose body resolved to nothing without listing it.

GET before every write and keep a persisted source-identity mapping, so a re-run creates no duplicates. Collection product_ids is a full replacement set — omit it until you know the complete mapped set, or you will silently empty a collection.

Products are already imported by the time this runs, so collection membership can resolve to real ids. Anything that cannot resolve goes in unresolved.

Keep page bodies out of your context: read what you need from the manifest and the clone-manifest, write each resource as you create it, and never hold a batch of fetched documents in the conversation. Exceeding the prompt limit is a hard failure that skips everything downstream.

Report pages as two numbers, not one. `pages` is the count with a non-empty body; `pages_empty` is the count published with nothing in it. A single record count hides the failure — 73 pages of which 52 are blank reads as a clean import.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { collections, categories, pages, pages_empty, posts, menus, empty_at_source: [...], body_from_rendered_dom: [...], membership_failures: [...], unresolved: [...] }.
acceptance: Every imported page has a non-empty body, or appears in empty_at_source with the rendered evidence that the source page is itself empty.
Pages whose body_html was empty were re-read from the rendered DOM before being written, and each one is listed in body_from_rendered_dom.
The page count reported in STEP_OUTPUT is the count of content-bearing pages, with blank publications reported separately as pages_empty.

steps.name: Pull in brand media and UGC
steps.prompt:
Stock the DAM with this brand's media, then with content other people made about it.

1. Brand's own: from the handles the brand step and the source site expose, pull the company's own recent social posts and video. Call run_skill("marketing/brand-social-import") and follow it.
2. Other people's: call run_skill("marketing/ugc-discovery") and follow it for UGC about the brand.

Run unattended. The UGC skill is written to let a human choose the keepers — you do not have one. Choose yourself: rank by engagement, keep the 8 to 20 best that are clearly about this brand and carry no health, income, or medical claim that would need FTC or FDA substantiation, and say what you rejected and why.

A company with no discoverable social presence is a valid, complete outcome. Report the queries you tried and finish — do not keep searching, and never wait for a person.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { brand_assets: <count>, ugc_assets: <count>, rejected: [{url, reason}], queries_attempted: [...], presence_found: true|false }.

steps.name: Review the storefront implementation
steps.prompt:
Review the published theme implementation from code and deterministic rendered evidence. This is a read-only audit: report findings and do not edit the theme. Screenshots and customer-click simulation are not correctness gates.

Read clone-manifest.json and inspect at least ten distinct implementation files across the shared shell, Home, Shop, Product, Collection, Cart, content, and system templates. Use at least six targeted searches to trace canonical template composition, stable copy, Fluid resource bindings, canonical links, product variant and add-to-cart hooks, cart state and totals, localization, and forbidden implementation shortcuts. Run fluid theme lint --json in read-only mode.

Treat the shared shell and every page file as read-only. Confirm the current code retains required canonical data sections, reuses the shared shell and existing contracts without duplicating or forking them, binds resources dynamically, avoids hardcoded environment identity and scaffold filler, contains no inline binary media or monolithic record-specific templates, and uses no layout-hiding workarounds. Do not claim which parallel step edited a file; this audit can judge only the current implementation.

Read rendered DOM in all mode for at least five distinct canonical routes from clone-manifest.json covering Home, Shop, one Product, one Collection, and Cart. Record HTTP status or expected themed error status, non-empty semantic output, stable copy, dynamic bindings when records exist, canonical links, localization, and shared-shell output. Read the preview console and local server logs for unresolved Liquid, runtime, resource, and browser errors.

Content import can still be running because storefront-check and import-content are concurrent. Missing content records or an empty data-dependent route is unresolved evidence, not automatically a theme-code failure; judge the bindings and available output, and state the missing prerequisite. DOM and code review do not prove viewport layout, horizontal overflow, image loading, interactive behavior, totals recomputation, or parity with API values. Do not take or compare screenshots, call view_project_image, or use interact_preview. Put unprovable behavior in unresolved rather than claiming it passed.

Separate findings by severity. Blocking means code or available deterministic evidence shows the storefront cannot render, navigate, bind core resources, add through the canonical purchase hooks, represent cart state, or reach checkout. Cosmetic means a non-blocking code-level mismatch. Do not promote missing concurrent data or unmeasured visual fidelity to a code defect.

You have no rework round and no write access, by design. Do not attempt, simulate, or promise a fix, and do not report inability to edit as a finding — remediation of everything you find belongs to the Theme project that owns these files. Your blocking list IS the handoff; make each entry specific enough to act on without you.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { files_read: [...], searches: [...], lint: {...}, routes: [{route, status, evidence: [...], issues: [...]}], console_errors: [...], server_errors: [...], blocking: [...], cosmetic: [...], unresolved: [...] }.
acceptance: The independent reviewer inspected clone-manifest.json and at least ten distinct implementation files spanning the shared shell, Home, Shop, Product, Collection, Cart, content, and system templates.
The independent reviewer ran fluid theme lint --json in read-only mode and it returned zero errors.

At least six targeted code searches traced canonical template composition, stable copy, Fluid resource bindings, canonical links, product purchase hooks, cart state/totals, localization, and forbidden implementation shortcuts.

Targeted code searches confirmed required canonical data sections remain present, the shared shell and existing contracts are reused without duplication or page-local forks, resource bindings remain dynamic, and no hardcoded environment identity, scaffold filler, inline binary media, monolithic record-specific template, or layout-hiding workaround is present.

The independent reviewer read rendered DOM in all mode for at least five distinct canonical routes covering Home, Shop, Product, Collection, and Cart, recording HTTP or expected themed error status, non-empty semantic output, dynamic bindings when records exist, canonical links, localization, and shared-shell output.
Missing records from concurrent import-content work are listed in unresolved and are not reported as a theme-code failure without code or rendered evidence.
The independent reviewer read the preview console and local server logs and found no unresolved Liquid, runtime, resource, or browser errors.

The reviewer did not claim that code or DOM proved viewport layout, horizontal overflow, image loading, interaction behavior, totals recomputation, or API-value parity, and did not use screenshot_preview, compare_preview_to_source, view_project_image, interact_preview, or screenshot-producing interaction checks as correctness evidence.
Findings are separated into blocking, cosmetic, and unresolved rather than presented as one undifferentiated list.

steps.name: What landed, and what needs you
steps.prompt:
Write the handoff a human reads first. Pull the STEP_OUTPUT of every step in this run; do not re-do their work and do not re-crawl the source site. Reading Fluid's own API to count what is live is not re-doing the work — it is the only way this summary can be true.

Every headline count is read live, not copied. A step's STEP_OUTPUT records what that step saw when it finished, before any later remediation — quoting it makes the handoff contradict the store it describes. Paginate the products and pages APIs for the counts you publish, and say `can_take_an_order` only after checking the live catalog and checkout, not because a step said so.

Lead with the live storefront URL and one honest sentence on whether this company could take an order today.

Then, in this order:
- What is live: theme, pages built, products and content imported, media in the DAM, with counts. Where a live count disagrees with the step that reported it, publish the live one and note the step it corrects.
- What is blocking: anything from the storefront check marked blocking, plus any step that finished needs-review, each with the one action that clears it.
- What is thin: fields left unresolved, pages skipped, fonts substituted, reputation not matched. These are follow-ups, not failures.
- What a human should confirm: brand.md was drafted from the public site and has never been seen by the company; the logo and palette were inferred; substituted fonts are a licensing decision.

Be specific and short. Counts, routes, and ids — not adjectives. If a step failed outright, say so plainly and say what is missing because of it.

End with STEP_OUTPUT: { live_url, can_take_an_order: true|false, live: {...}, counts_source: "live-api", corrected_step_counts: [...], blocking: [...], thin: [...], confirm_with_human: [...] }.
acceptance: Every count in the handoff was read from the live API in this step, not copied from an earlier step's STEP_OUTPUT.
can_take_an_order reflects the live catalog and checkout rather than a step's self-report.
